newsitem.title: USA: Compaq cuts PC prices by up to 23 percent.
newsitem.headline: Compaq cuts PC prices by up to 23 percent.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp on Monday said it will cut prices by up to 23 percent on its business desktop personal computers, notebooks and handheld PCs, and networking products.
This is the third round of cuts announced this year by Compaq, the global PC sales leader.
The company said the price cuts were enacted in a move to extend its marketshare lead.
Compaq also dropped prices on PC options and introduced or extended several promotions linked to the purchase of new PCs.

The company said it cut prices by up to 23 percent across the entire line of Compaq Deskpro PCs, between 13 and 29 percent on its Armada 4100, LTE 5000 notebook PCs and PC companion portable product lines, and as much as 22 percent price on select Netelligent communications products.
Compaq said a Deskpro 2000 entry-level business PC, configured with a 133 MHz Pentium processor, 1.2 Gigabyte hard drive and 16 megabytes of memory, will now start at $1,070.

Compaq lowered prices 11 to 16 percent on its line of Professional Workstations. A Professional Workstation 5000 equipped with a 200 MHz Pentium Pro processor, 32 megabytes of memory and a two gigabyte hard drive now starts at $3,500.
Its LTE 5000 high-performance notebook personal computers will now start at about $3,399, the company said.
The company did not specify what the starting price of the computers were previously.
